reproduced_numbers:
Fresh scratch copy at .../verify-retention-classifier/{base,repo}. The designer's f3.diff applies cleanly and gives the same md5s as frozen_md5.txt.

LongMemEval dev, official replay/summarize, 92 examples (87 with gold):
- memory_retention 21.26% -> 90.96%
- mean visible_fraction 17.48% -> 54.90%
- bytes after cleanup 3,122,879 -> 3,529,654
- cleanup preserved the visible state in 92 of 92 examples
- Every per-type number matches the designer's table exactly.

Held-out, re-run by me as the verifier with no tuning, 365 examples (349 with gold):
- retention 20.97% -> 90.45%
- visible 18.33% -> 55.29%
- Overlap-free subset (347 examples sharing no verbatim user turn with dev): 21.23% -> 90.74%.

Rule trace on base dev user turns, as (non-gold, gold): '?' (654, 89), hedge (50, 21), fallback (43, 5). Matches the designer.

60 held-out classification cases:
- category accuracy 50.0% -> 53.3%
- macro-F1 0.516 -> 0.544
- tier accuracy 55.0% -> 56.7%
- 11 cases changed, all temporary -> episodic, none went from correct to wrong.

Other checks:
- evaluation.lifecycle: 16/16 before and after.
- pytest on the patched copy: 168 passed, 136 subtests passed.
- Legacy check re-run on the frozen code (20,660 inputs): the hashes for legacy category, legacy features, ML features and the with_ml record (category, features, score, tier) are identical. Only the with_ml expiry hash differs, as the designer disclosed.

Simpler alternative, dev only (every non-phatic user turn becomes EPISODIC, no self_disclosure regex): retention 90.96% (same), visible 60.9% (vs 54.9%). The regex buys about 6pp of selectivity at no recall cost on dev.

Remaining held-out misses (patched, 53 total):
- 31 user EPISODIC turns older than 90 days
- 14 assistant turns
- 5 user turns lost to self_disclosure false negatives (out of 616 gold user turns)
- 3 user task turns

Regression found:
- Relation-bearing gold memories run through MemoryCore with the clock pinned to each memory's timestamp: base 150 of 192 are SEMANTIC/long_term with no expiry. Patched, only 81 are; 69 become EPISODIC/short_term with 90-day expiry.
- End to end: "I'm at Acme now." with a works_at relation is returned by search at day 120 in base, but the patched build returns no hits (the graph edge still exists).
- A one-line guard restores 150 of 150, leaves dev retention at 90.96% / 54.90%, and all 168 tests still pass.

issues.issue: An unintended regression in the graph pipeline. core.process upgrades a user input to SEMANTIC (long_term, no expiry) when it carries explicit relations metadata and the classifier returned TEMPORARY. The new S1/S2 paths now return EPISODIC for these inputs first, so the upgrade never fires. Explicitly structured facts (allergies, residence, employer, relationships) become EPISODIC/short_term and expire after 90 days, and retrieval then stops returning them. The risks section does not mention this, and no test or benchmark covers it, because the ablation and LoCoMo both load frozen SEMANTIC records.
issues.evidence:
main/application/core.py:62-64 only upgrades when `category is MemoryCategory.TEMPORARY`.
Processing the 456 gold memories through MemoryCore with the clock pinned to each memory's created_at (scripts/gold_proc2.py), 192 carry relations:
- base: 150 are SEMANTIC/long_term with no expiry
- patched: only 81 are; 69 are EPISODIC/short_term with 90-day expiry
Examples: 'Shellfish is the one thing I really can't eat, I break out in hives within minutes.' (allergy relation) and "I've been renting a tiny flat in Lisbon since 2021...".
End to end (scripts/rel_e2e.py): "I'm at Acme now." with a works_at relation, query 'Where does Sam work?':
- day 30: hit in both base and patched
- day 120: base still returns it; patched returns hits=[] even though graph_edges=1
The guard `not memory_input.metadata.get('relations')` in _discloses restores 150 of 150 SEMANTIC/long_term. Dev retention is unchanged (90.96% / 54.90%) and 168 tests pass.

issues.issue: The 90-day horizon applies to every user EPISODIC short_term record, not only the newly kept disclosures. User task-update and event observations (task_action and event_update paths) also move from 14 to 90 days. The proposal's wording ('every other short-term memory keeps 14 days') and the test that shows the 14-day window (it uses role='assistant' for 'I submitted my report today.') understate this. With role='user', the same text now gets 90 days.
issues.evidence:
scripts/task.py, user role, base -> patched:
- 'Move the dentist appointment to Friday': 14 days -> 90 days
- 'I finished the quarterly report.': 14 days -> 90 days
- 'I submitted my report today.': 14 days -> 90 days
main/domain/lifecycle.py:57 keys only on role == 'user' and category EPISODIC.

issues.issue: The lifecycle change also alters the with_ml and with_neural pipelines. User EPISODIC records from the legacy classifier now expire after 90 days. Feature preprocessing, scores and tiers are unchanged, and the designer disclosed this, but the ML pipelines' retention policy is no longer what it was.
issues.evidence: My re-run of legacy_check.py on the frozen code: the category, legacy_features, ml_features and with_ml_record_no_expiry hashes match base. Only with_ml_expiry differs (base 7d79715f..., patched dc2b9898...).

issues.issue:
self_disclosure has false positives and depends on exact phrasing. Its selectivity is shown only on probes the designer wrote and partly developed against.
- 'i.e.', a code variable `i`, roman numerals ('type I', 'Elizabeth I'), generic we/our ('Is it true that we only use 10% of our brain?'), hypotheticals ('If I invest $1000...'), role-play ('Pretend I am a pirate') and single-quoted quotations are all kept for 90 days. Single quotes are never stripped; only double quotes are.
- Near-paraphrases split: 'Do I need a visa for Japan?' stays TEMPORARY, but 'Do you know if I need a visa to visit Japan?' becomes EPISODIC.
- On LongMemEval the regex adds only about 6pp of selectivity compared with the simplest rule (keep every non-phatic user turn).
issues.evidence:
scripts/adv.py outputs:
- episodic/90d for 'What vegetables grow in shade, i.e. leafy greens?', 'Can you fix this loop? for i in range(10): print(i)', 'What is the difference between type I and type II diabetes?', 'Who succeeded Elizabeth I?', "Write a poem that starts with 'I wandered lonely as a cloud'.", 'Pretend I am a pirate and talk to me.'
- temporary for 'Do I need a visa for Japan?'
scripts/alt.py on dev: the non-phatic rule gives 90.96% retention at 60.9% visible, vs 90.96% at 54.9% for the regex.

issues.issue: Hedged statements and role-play that used to expire after 1 hour now persist for 90 days and appear in retrieval results. They never become claims and rank below the asserted fact in my probes, but they reach top-k and the answer context. This is a precision cost that the retention metric cannot see, because keep-everything scores 100%.
issues.evidence:
scripts/e2e.py, top-3 at day 5, patched:
- 'Where do I live?' returns 'I live in Pune.' first, then 'I might move to Mumbai next year...'
- 'What do I eat?' returns "I'm vegetarian." first, then 'Pretend I am a cowboy who loves steak...'
In base, only the fact appears. Base also loses "I'm vegetarian." entirely, which the patch fixes.

issues.issue: A small leakage concern with no measurable effect. The `world war i` special case in _NON_DISCLOSING matches LongMemEval text only in the held-out split (0 dev hits, 6 held-out). The two splits are disjoint by question_id, but 18 held-out examples share verbatim user turns with dev.
issues.evidence:
scripts/grep_split.py: 'world war i' gives dev=0, heldout=6. The only held-out user turn changes nothing either way (episodic with or without the clause, has_answer=False).
scripts/overlap.py: 25 of 616 held-out gold user turns appear verbatim in dev. On the overlap-free held-out subset, retention is 21.23% -> 90.74%, the same as the full set.
Timeline check: the held-out runs (01:51:24 and 01:51:33) come after frozen_md5 (01:50:58), and no code was edited afterwards.

issues.issue: Process and documentation gaps. The designer's legacy byte-identity check (01:45) and sub-change ablation (01:42) ran before the last edit to text_rules.py (01:50:58). I re-ran the legacy check on the frozen code and it holds. README.md still says short-term memories expire after fourteen days.
issues.evidence: File mtimes in the designer's out/ directory. README.md:69: 'Working memory normally expires after one hour, short-term after fourteen days'.

recommended_adjustments:
The core idea is sound and the numbers are real. Classifying first-person user questions and hedges as EPISODIC observations, never claims, and keeping them for 90 days takes LongMemEval retention from 21% to 90%, on both dev and held-out, with no leakage that changes the result. Make these changes before merging:

1. (Required) Restore the relations-to-SEMANTIC upgrade. One option is to guard the disclosure path in `MemoryClassifier._discloses`:
   `return memory_input.role == 'user' and not memory_input.metadata.get('relations') and self_disclosure(memory_input.content)`
   The other is to widen the condition in core.process (lines 62-64) so it also covers disclosure-derived EPISODIC. Either way, add a regression test, e.g. \"I'm at Acme now.\" with a works_at relation should be SEMANTIC/long_term with no expiry. I verified the guard version: it restores 150 of 150 SEMANTIC relation memories, keeps dev at 90.96% / 54.90%, and all 168 tests pass.

2. Scope the 90-day horizon to what the fix is about, or document the wider scope. Currently user task-update and event observations also get 90 days. Option (a): only records whose category came from S1/S2 get 90 days, e.g. by setting source_metadata['retention_reason'] = 'user_disclosure' and checking it in LifecycleManager. Option (b): keep the broad rule, but fix the claim that 'every other short-term memory keeps 14 days', and test the 14-day case with a user-role, non-disclosure example rather than an assistant one.

3. If the with_ml and with_neural pipelines must stay frozen end to end, give LifecycleManager a flag (e.g. user_event_days=None for the ML cores) so their expiry stays at 14 days.

4. Low-risk precision cleanups to self_disclosure:
   - also strip single-quoted spans
   - drop 'i.e.' and similar abbreviations
   - match the pronoun I on the original casing, so a lowercase code variable `i` no longer counts
   - replace the held-out-only 'world war i' special case with a general rule: uppercase I after a capitalised word or 'type'/'part'/'war'/'phase' is a numeral
   - treat 'pretend' and 'suppose' role-play as non-disclosing

   Tune any of these on dev or probes only. Alternatively, state that the simpler rule (every non-phatic user turn becomes EPISODIC) reaches the same dev retention at +6pp visible, and keep the regex only if the extra selectivity is worth its upkeep.

5. Update README.md (line 69) to describe the new short-term windows.

6. Before claiming any end-to-end benefit, measure the precision cost of retaining hedges and role-play for 90 days on a QA or retrieval task built from LongMemEval dev. The retention metric rewards keep-everything and cannot show this cost.
